# QA feedback — record findings

Document a manual-verification finding into
`qa-manual-verification/999-qa-feedback.md`. This skill *produces* the file that
[[qa-address-issues]] later consumes, so keep both halves of that file — the
detailed **finding card** and the one-line **global register** — in sync. The
flows being walked come from [[qa-identify-scenarios]].

## What this skill does

For each finding the user reports while walking the
`qa-manual-verification/NNN-*.md` scenarios:

1. Append a filled **finding card** to the **Findings** section.
2. Add a matching one-line row to the **global register of findings** table.
3. Mirror it into the relevant scenario file's "Feedback / hallazgos" table when
   the finding belongs to a concrete scenario (that scenario table keeps its
   existing Spanish columns).

Do not invent findings. Capture only what the user observed; if a required field
is unknown, ask one focused question or leave a clear `n/a` / `pending`.

## The feedback file

`qa-manual-verification/999-qa-feedback.md` has two parts you keep in sync: the
**Global register of findings** table (one row per finding) and the **Findings**
section (one finding card per bug). If that file does not exist yet, create it
from the `999-qa-feedback.md` template shipped in this skill's folder — it
already has both empty sections and the legend — then append into it. Add new
cards at the end of the **Findings** section and new rows at the end of the
register; never overwrite the headings.

## ID assignment

- Read the existing **global register** table first and pick the next free
  `BUG-NNN` (zero-padded to 3 digits: `BUG-001`, `BUG-002`, …).
- The card `ID` and the register row `ID` must match exactly.

## Severities

- `blocker` — blocks the flow.
- `high` — breaks an important feature, workaround exists.
- `medium` — works badly but does not block.
- `low` — minor annoyance.
- `cosmetic` — text/style.

## Finding card template (one per bug)

Copy this block verbatim and fill it in. Keep the literal field labels in bold so
both humans and [[qa-address-issues]] can parse it.

```markdown
### Bug NNNN

**ID:** `BUG-NNN`
**Date:** `YYYY-MM-DD`
**Severity:** `blocker | high | medium | low | cosmetic`
**Scenario & step:** `(e.g. 028 — Email catalog, step 6 "Instant alert")`

**What you expected:**
> …

**What you observed:**
> … (include literal error messages, HTTP codes, email subject/`template_name`,
> etc.)

**How to reproduce:**

1. …
2. …
3. …

**Environment:**

- Browser / version: `(e.g. Chrome 126)`
- Session: `no session | Free | Pro | team (role)`
- Active flags: `(checkout off, empresas deferred, …)`
- Jobs run before: `(e.g. official-source, adjudicaciones)`

**Screenshot / attachment:** `(link or filename; redact sensitive info)`

**Suspect path or file:** `(e.g. api/src/app/api/team.py, web/src/proxy.ts)`

**Possible issue / technical note:**
> … (root-cause hypothesis, related issue, whether it is a known PRD divergence)
```

Use today's date for **Date** (the harness provides `currentDate`). Redact any
sensitive data from screenshots and reproduction steps.

## Global register row

Add one row per finding to the table under "Global register of findings". A new
finding always starts with status `open`:

```markdown
| BUG-NNN | <severity> | <NNN scenario> | <one-line summary> | open |
```

Valid statuses (the lifecycle owned by [[qa-address-issues]]):
`open` · `in review` · `confirmed` · `dismissed` · `resolved`.

When recording, only ever set `open`. Do not advance the status here — status
transitions belong to the [[qa-address-issues]] workflow.

## Guardrails

- Edit only `qa-manual-verification/999-qa-feedback.md` (creating it from the
  shipped template if absent) and, when relevant, the per-scenario `NNN-*.md`
  "Feedback / hallazgos" table. Do not touch application code from this skill.
- Keep the register table and the cards consistent: every register row has a card
  with the same `ID`, and vice versa.
- Do not commit unless the user asks; recording a finding is a working-tree edit.
